messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging eng-oncall: high KV cache evictions and continuous-batching amplification observed for prod region eu-west-1. Impact: elevated tail latency and increased token cost. Investigating.
Kai: seeing a big jump in kv-cache-misses over the last 7m. QPS hasn't changed much but batch sizes doubled.
maria: logs show repeated shard contention errors on cache-shard-12, evictions spike at 12:07 UTC. Exporting a tail of logs now.
simon: adding context — we shipped the new batching heuristic yesterday (batch-window-adaptive) at 22:00 UTC for all hosted customers. Possibly correlated.
jamal: @simon can we toggle the heuristic back quickly? We should consider canary rollback or pinning per-tenant.
ops-bot: Autoscaling check: GPU pool eu-west-1 has headroom, no provisioning failures detected.
rohit: interesting — autoscaler healthy but eviction rate suggests memory pressure in the per-shard KV layer, not overall infra.
Kai: copying the hot traces:
```
[2026-03-15T12:06:58Z] shard=12 mem_used=93% evictions=842 rps=120 batch_mean=18 batch_p99=240
[2026-03-15T12:07:10Z] shard=12 lock_wait=120ms kv_cache_miss=0.42
```
Kai: batch_p99 at 240 tokens — that's way up from baseline ~16.
maria: customer impacts: increased latency for chat route /v1/chat and some timed-out requests for tenants with long seqs. No full outages reported yet.
simon: plan proposal: 1) pause adaptive batching for prod via feature flag; 2) enable per-tenant override for highest-traffic customers; 3) roll a small canary of the revert first.
jamal: agree. I'll prepare flag flips. Which flag exactly? `batch-window-adaptive-enabled`? rohit: yes that's it. Default true.
Kai: recommend canary sequence: 1) disable for 5% of hosts (non-critical), 2) if stable -> 25% 3) then full. But for impacted tenants do immediate per-tenant disable.
kayla: list of top impacted tenants from recent alerts: acme-corp, leafly-inc, beta-shop. We should target overrides for those.
ops-bot: Creating on-call incident doc: https://redwood/infra/incidents/2912345678 (placeholder)
jamal: executing first step — canary disable on 5%:
```
rdctl flags set batch-window-adaptive-enabled false --env prod --percent 5
```
jamal: done. flag change propagated to 5% of serving nodes at 12:13 UTC.
Kai: metrics after 3 minutes: batch p99 for canary hosts down to 18. Overall still high due to remaining hosts.
simon: good signal. Next, per-tenant override for acme-corp and beta-shop immediately.
jamal: applying per-tenant override:
```
rdctl flags set batch-window-adaptive-enabled false --env prod --tenant acme-corp
rdctl flags set batch-window-adaptive-enabled false --env prod --tenant beta-shop
```
jamal: applied at 12:18 UTC.
maria: acme-corp latency dropped to baseline within ~60s. beta-shop similar. Their errors decreased to 0.1% from 2.8%.
rohit: why are two tenants enough to show such big total cost? because they have many long-sequence streams hitting the cache hot shards.
Kai: next: broaden the canary to 25% while we keep per-tenant overrides for the big ones.
jamal: executing:
```
rdctl flags set batch-window-adaptive-enabled false --env prod --percent 25
```
jamal: propagated at 12:24 UTC.
Kai: monitoring dashboards: overall p99 token latency down ~40% in the last 6m. Evictions trending down.
simon: ok, let's keep the canary at 25% for 15 minutes to ensure no regression from other dimensions (throughput, avg latency, cold-starts).
kayla: notifications out to SEs for impacted customers. CCing support to confirm no functional regressions from the flag change.
Kai: quick root-cause hypothesis: the new adaptive window increases batch window size aggressively when seq_len distribution skews long, causing caches to fill KV entries for many prefixes, leading to shard-local memory pressure and eviction cascades.
rohit: also saw lock contention on shard metadata updates when batch sizes spike — explains lock_wait >100ms.
simon: follow-ups: 1) revert the heuristic to a safer algorithm (less aggressive expansion), 2) implement shard-level admission control, 3) add per-tenant pseudo-quotas to prevent a tenant from expanding batch sizes across too many shards.
jamal: creating a PR for immediate safe revert — will ship hotfix to canary hosts first.
jamal: PR link: https://git.redwood/eng/runtime/pulls/4862
jamal: launching staged deploy to canary at 12:35 UTC. command:
```
deployctl rollout runtime-adaptive-revert --env prod --group canary
```
ops-bot: Deploy started: runtime-adaptive-revert -> canary group
Kai: observing canary deploy metrics — so far stable, no error spike. Batch mean normalized.
rohit: note: we should keep per-tenant overrides documented for SRE on how to flip quickly — adding runbook snippet.
Maria: runbook snippet:
```
# quick per-tenant feature flag toggle
rdctl flags set <flag> <value> --env prod --tenant <tenant-id>
# verify:
rdctl flags get <flag> --env prod --tenant <tenant-id>
```
kayla: support confirms acme-corp engineering saw no data loss and are satisfied with performance improvement.
Kai: after 20m of canary stability we'll roll to 100% and then mark incident as mitigated.
simon: I'll own the postmortem. Assigning action items: rohit (kernel/lock fix), jamal (revert PR + rollback automation), kai (observability alerts tweak), maria (customer comms + impact timeline).
incident-bot: Incident status updated -> mitigation in place. Next update in 30m unless changes.
jamal: rolling to 100% now at 12:54 UTC with `deployctl rollout runtime-adaptive-revert --env prod --group all`.
ops-bot: Deploy completed: runtime-adaptive-revert -> all. 12:58 UTC.
Kai: final checks: p99 stable, evictions back to baseline, token cost trending down. Closing live mitigation phase.
kayla: sending wrap-up to SEs + customer success. Preparing a concise summary.
maria: adding timeline to incident doc and flag flips + per-tenant list.
simon: thanks team. Postmortem draft expected EOD. If anyone sees a reoccurence ping immediately in this thread.
